EPACK : TERMINATES JVA WITH BUMJIN ELECTRONICS OF KOREA

• Bumjin Korea did not subscribe to any shares of Bumjin India and the JV did not proceed as envisaged
• Bumjin India remains a wholly owned subsidiary of the Company and has not commenced business operations
• Company, as sole shareholder, to undertake strike-off of Bumjin India at its own cost

SUMEETINDS : CRISIL REAFFIRMS BB+/STABLE RATING ON RS 292 CR BANK FACILITIES

• Long-term bank facilities reaffirmed at CRISIL BB+/Stable; short-term facilities reaffirmed at CRISIL A4+
• Total bank loan facilities rated at ₹292 Cr across cash credit, LC/bank guarantee and term loans
• FY26 revenue rose to ₹1,050.42 Cr from ₹1,003.51 Cr in FY25; H1 FY27 revenue around ₹636 Cr
• EBITDA margin improved to 5.54% in FY26 from 1.25% in FY25, but moderated to around 3.11% in Q1 FY27 on higher raw material costs
• ₹199.75 Cr rights issue in FY27 lifted networth to ₹183.9 Cr as on March 31, 2026; gearing at 1.04 times, interest coverage 5.79 times vs 3.49 times
• Liquidity adequate with bank limit utilisation at 77.44% average for 12 months to September 2026; capex of around ₹165 Cr under implementation
Impact: Positive (reaffirmation keeps bank funding access intact, though profitability remains exposed to PTA and MEG price swings)

**APTUS VALUE HOUSING FINANCE – BROKERAGE UPDATE**

**JEFFERIES: BUY | TARGET ₹290**
- Earlier target: ₹350.
- FY27 AUM growth expected at 20%.
- Management guidance stands at 22%.
- Subsidiary stress and borrowing costs threaten margins.
- FY27–28 EPS estimates cut 1–3%.
- 19–20% ROE supports outlook.

**NIVA BUPA – BROKERAGE UPDATE**

**JEFFERIES: BUY | TARGET ₹100**
- Earlier target: ₹95.
- Retail health growth and market-share gains support expansion.
- Improving claims ratios and new products support profitability.
- FY28–29 earnings estimates raised 5–12%.
- Regulations and solvency remain monitorables.

**TORRENT POWER – BROKERAGE UPDATE**

**JEFFERIES: BUY | TARGET ₹1,635**
- Earlier target: ₹1,780.
- Renewable capacity target: 10 GW by FY30.
- FY27 additions planned: 1–1.2 GW.
- FY30 EBITDA CAGR: 13%.
- Renewable EBITDA growth expected at 35%.
- Transmission bottlenecks and execution delays remain risks.
- Pumped storage offers additional potential.

REDINGTON – Q2 FY27 CONCALL HIGHLIGHTS

GROWTH OUTLOOK
- H2 FY27 revenue growth expected above 25%.
- Strong AI infrastructure demand expected.
- Apple volumes expected to recover in Q4.

COST & CAPITAL
- Quarterly OPEX guidance: ₹950–1,000 Cr.
- Evaluating potential capital raise.

IOL Chemicals & Pharmaceuticals | Key Takeaways from Q2 FY27 Concall

-  Business Diversification: Non-ibuprofen APIs are gaining traction, while backward integration in ibuprofen and expansion into formulations are expected to strengthen the company's API business and improve value addition.

 ₹500 Cr Capex Programme: Major investments in ibuprofen capacity, formulation CDMO and specialty chemicals are aimed at expanding manufacturing capabilities and driving export-led growth over the coming years.

Growth Outlook & Monitorables: Management expects H2 performance to remain broadly similar to H1. Key monitorables include capex execution, CDMO customer approvals, utilisation ramp-up and working capital discipline.

Q2FY26 Concalls Highlights
@Concalls3

APOLLO HOSPITALS – SUNEETA REDDY
KEY MANAGEMENT COMMENTARY

HOSPITALS BUSINESS
- EBITDA margin contracted 60 bps.
- New bed commissioning impacted margins.
- Retains hospital growth guidance of 18–20%.

ONCOLOGY BUSINESS
- Oncology contributes 21% of total revenue.
- Limited impact expected from 30% drug trade margin cap.

INDRAPRASTHA HOSPITAL
- Awaiting court decision on Indraprastha Hospital.

INDUSTRY OUTLOOK
- Seeks stronger government and public representation.
- Emphasises the importance of hospitals.

**LUPIN – BROKERAGE UPDATE**

**JEFFERIES: UNDERPERFORM | TARGET ₹1,750**
- Earlier target: ₹2,050.
- US sales expected to decline.
- Mirabegron and Tolvaptan face intensifying competition.
- Major respiratory, injectable and biosimilar launches unlikely before FY29.
- FY27–28 EPS estimates cut 5% and 1%.
- FY27 EBITDA margin guidance: 24–25%.

MANISHI RAYCHAUDHURI – EMMER CAPITAL
CNBC-TV18 – KEY MARKET VIEWS

FII FLOWS
- Early signs of FII flows returning to EMs.
- Chinese stocks witnessing sharp rallies.
- Large frontline stocks likely attract FIIs.

BANKING SECTOR
- Private banks expected to gain market share.
- NIMs expected to benefit from interest rate hikes.

SECTOR PREFERENCES
- Positive on industrials and capital goods.
- Also favours banking stocks.

STOCK-SPECIFIC VIEWS
- Reliance has multiple growth drivers.
- Significant embedded value remains.

INDIAN IT SECTOR
- AI value proposition remains strong.
- IT disruption risks cannot be ignored.

DR. REDDY'S LABORATORIES – GENERIC SEMAGLUTIDE APPROVAL IN BRAZIL

REGULATORY APPROVAL
- Brazil's ANVISA approves generic semaglutide injection.
- Indicated for adults with uncontrolled Type 2 diabetes.
- Once-weekly dosing formulation.

PRODUCT DETAILS
- Pre-filled, multi-dose injectable pen.
- Available in 2 mg/1.5 mL presentation.
- Also available in 4 mg/3 mL presentation.

MARKET OPPORTUNITY
- Brazil's diabetes semaglutide market: ~$244.6 Mn.

LAUNCH PLANS
- Dr. Reddy's plans Brazilian product launch.
- Launch planned in partnership with Aché.

- EBITDA margin guidance raised above 28%.

- Targets 10,000+ India stores by 2030.

- Expects continued YoY margin expansion.

- Volume growth target: 8–10%.
- Assumes spice inflation moderates to 5–7%.
- September price hike benefits Q3 margins.
- Kerala distribution restructuring by March 2027.
- Expanding digital commerce and wet batter.
- Focus on convenience foods.

**GOLDMAN SACHS: NEUTRAL | TARGET ₹485**
- Premium brands growing 4x faster.
- Haircare, digestives and beverages drive growth.
- CEO transition, input costs and honey demand remain monitorables.

**HSBC: HOLD | TARGET ₹426**
- Leadership transition puts strategy under focus.
- General trade, haircare and beverages support growth.

**MACQUARIE: NEUTRAL | TARGET ₹480**
- Premiumisation supports portfolio growth.
- Beverages, digestives and international markets offer opportunities.
- Limited volume acceleration and FSSAI risks constrain outlook.

**JEFFERIES: BUY | TARGET ₹535**

- Rural recovery, premiumisation and Project Saksham support growth.
- Healthcare faces regulatory challenges.

- Eastgate Secondaries fundraising target: ₹1,500 Cr.
- ₹690 Cr cash supports ₹8,000 Cr fund sponsorship.

IND-SWIFT LABORATORIES – Q2 FY27 CONCALL HIGHLIGHTS

- FY27 revenue growth target: 50%+.
- Q4 EBITDA margin target: 20–22%.
- Incremental CDMO revenue target: ₹100–130 Cr.
- FY30 revenue target: ₹1,500 Cr+.

**JPMORGAN – INDIA SECTOR OPPORTUNITIES**

**Power & Infrastructure**
- FY36 peak electricity demand: 459 GW.
- Current demand: 271 GW.
- Transmission investment opportunity: ₹8 lakh Cr.

**Valuations & Opportunities**
- MSCI India trades 13.4% below 10-year average.
- Banks, real estate, insurance and materials offer value.
- Lower crude benefits aviation, paints, cement, tyres and logistics.

**Key Risks**
- El Niño and weak rainfall threaten rural demand.

DR LAL PATHLABS – Q2 FY27 CONCALL HIGHLIGHTS

- FY27 revenue growth guidance: High-teens.
- EBITDA margin expected above FY26's 28.3%.
- Plans 15–18 new labs in FY27.
- Price hike possible within 1–2 quarters.
- Further expansion through acquisitions.

LUPIN – Q2 FY27 CONCALL HIGHLIGHTS

- FY27 US revenue guidance: $1.1–1.2 Bn.
- FY27 EBITDA margin guidance: 24–25%.
- Guidance maintained despite Tolvaptan competition.
- FY28 US revenue target: $1 Bn+.
- Long-term EBITDA margin target: 29–30%.
- Plans 60+ US launches over three years.

**JPMORGAN – INDIA EQUITY STRATEGY**

**Market Outlook**
- Bullish on Indian equities.
- Falling crude, US yields support sentiment.
- FII reversal could unlock $115 billion inflows.
- Lower crude supports rupee and corporate margins.
- Small/midcaps expected to outperform largecaps.

**Sector Allocation**
- Overweight: Financials, Industrials, Healthcare.
- Overweight: Materials, Consumer Discretionary.
- Underweight: IT.

**Growth Opportunities**
- Private capex recovery gaining momentum.
- Opportunities: Renewables, semiconductors, EVs, data centres.

- Order value: INR 1628.74 Cr

text:
**Arvind Fashions

A few interesting commitments:

→ Mid-double-digit revenue growth for the balance of FY27
→ 30–40 bps EBITDA margin expansion
→ D2C share target of ~65%, from 53% currently
→ H2 free cash flow release of ₹150–175 crore, with a large part intended for debt reduction.
Growth, channel mix and balance-sheet improvement. Worth tracking together.**

**Carborundum Universal Q2

A good example of why segment-level analysis matters.

FY27 guidance:

→ Ceramics growth raised to 25–28%
→ Ceramics margin raised to 22.5–23.5%
→ Abrasives margin lowered to 8–8.5%.
Different segments, different trajectories. Consolidated numbers may not tell the complete story.**

**Tanfac Industries Q2

Management raised FY27 revenue growth guidance from 30% to 35–40%.

The bigger story is HFC-32:

→ 2,000–3,000 tonnes volume ramp-up in FY27
→ ~95% utilisation targeted in FY28
→ FY28 EBITDA margin guidance: 24–26%.
A significant capacity ramp-up lies ahead.**

**Dhoot Transmission Q2 

Strong growth ambitions:

→ FY27 revenue growth: 40–45%
→ FY27 capex: ~₹750 crore
→ EBITDA margin: 15–16%
→ Three additional wiring harness plants expected by mid-FY28.
Now, execution and utilisation will be key to watch.**

**GNG Electronics

Management raised its FY27 revenue growth guidance to ~40%.
PAT margin expansion guidance also improved from 100 bps to 150 bps over FY26.
One thing to watch: inventory is expected to remain elevated through Q4 FY27.**

**PRABHUDAS LILLADHER – INDRAPRASTHA GAS (IGL)**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target price revised to ₹161 from ₹165.

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- EBITDA loss: ₹30 Cr.
- EBITDA missed estimates significantly.
- EBITDA/scm: -₹0.30 vs ₹3.40 in Q1.
- Gas costs increased 22% QoQ, 47.9% YoY.

**Volume Performance**
- Total volumes: 10.1 mmscmd, up 8% YoY.
- CNG volumes: 7.6 mmscmd, up 8.7%.
- PNG volumes: 2.5 mmscmd, up 6%.
- Total volumes grew 4.2% QoQ.

**Margin & Supply Outlook**
- Spot LNG share increased to 15% from 3%.
- Management retains ₹6–7/scm EBITDA guidance.
- Term LNG supplies expected from Q3.
- Further supply additions expected during Q4.
- Targets approximately 10% volume growth.

**Valuation**
- Standalone business valued at 10x Sep'28E EPS.
- Investments valued at ₹21/share.
- Holding company discount: 25%.

**Key Takeaway**
- Higher spot gas costs severely impacted margins.
- Strong volume growth remains encouraging.
- Term LNG recovery is the key catalyst.
- Impact: **Mixed to Positive**

**NOMURA – STATE BANK OF INDIA (SBI)**

- Asset quality remained benign.

**Key Takeaway**
- NIM expansion supported NII outperformance.
- One-time gains supported reported earnings.
- Slower growth and higher costs remain concerns.
- Impact: **Neutral**

**CITI – STATE BANK OF INDIA (SBI)**

**Rating & Target Price**

- Target price: ₹1,300.

- PAT: ₹23,000 Cr, up 14% YoY.
- Stake-sale gain: ₹7,290 Cr.
- Treasury loss: ₹1,280 Cr.
- Operating expenses rose 15% YoY, 38% QoQ.
- NII grew 14% YoY, 4.6% QoQ.
- NII exceeded estimates.
- NIM expanded 8bps QoQ.
- Estimates had projected a 2bps decline.

**NIM & Loan Growth Outlook**
- 49% of loans linked to external benchmarks.
- 32% of loans are repo-linked.
- Rising rates could support NIMs.
- Management retained 3%+ NIM guidance.
- Loan growth: 18.2% YoY, 3.3% QoQ.
- Corporate lending remained flat.
- FY27 advances guidance: 14–15%.
- Citi expects loan growth above 16%.

- Credit costs remained below 0.35%.
- ECL transition impact: ₹19,500 Cr.
- Equivalent to 3.3% of net worth.
- Equivalent to 0.4% of advances.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong NII and NIM recovery support earnings.
- Stake-sale gains boosted reported PAT.
- Loan growth remains a key monitorable.
- Asset quality remains healthy.
- Impact: **Positive**

- Loan growth remained relatively lower.

- Target price reduced despite EPS upgrades.

- Strong NIM momentum supports earnings outlook.
- Operating leverage provides additional earnings support.
- Slower loan growth limits valuation upside.
- Impact: **Positive**

- Distribution income contributes below 3% of PBT.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong NII growth supported by NIM expansion.
- Broad-based domestic loan growth remains healthy.
- Improving asset quality supports earnings visibility.
- Impact: **Positive**

**GOLDMAN SACHS – MARICO LIMITED**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target price: ₹950.

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- Results exceeded estimates.
- Quality of growth remained strong.
- Double-digit volume growth sustained.
- Parachute volume growth: 13% YoY.
- VAHO sustained strong growth.

**Business Performance**
- Saffola edible-oil portfolio reset continues.
- Strong volume growth supports business momentum.

**Growth Outlook**
- FY27 growth guidance upgraded.
- Medium-term growth outlook upgraded.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong volumes and quality growth.
- Parachute and VAHO drive momentum.
- Guidance upgrades signal confidence.
- Impact: **Positive**

**JPMORGAN – MARICO LIMITED**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Overweight.
- Target price: ₹940.

**Q2 FY27 Financial Performance**
- Revenue growth: 13% YoY.
- EBITDA growth: 27% YoY.
- PAT growth: 29% YoY.

**India Business Performance**
- Domestic volume growth: 10%.
- Parachute volume growth: 13%.
- Parachute recorded highest growth in 22 quarters.
- Mid/premium VAHO delivered mid-teens growth.
- Foods and PPC continued scaling up.
- Digital brands expanded with improving profitability.

**International Business**
- International growth: 13% constant currency.
- Bangladesh continued facing soft business trends.
- Management expects gradual Bangladesh recovery.
- Recovery expected to support H2 performance.

**EBITDA Growth Drivers**
- Sustained volume growth.
- Improving portfolio mix.
- Lower copra costs.
- Strong EBITDA expansion despite higher brand investments.

**FY27 Guidance**
- EBITDA growth guidance raised to mid-20s.
- Minimum growth guidance: 24–25%.
- Earlier guidance: Around 20%.
- Better cost visibility supports upgraded guidance.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong volumes drive operational momentum.
- Portfolio mix and lower copra costs support margins.
- Growth businesses improve profitability.
- Impact: **Positive**

**CLSA – MARICO LIMITED**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating upgraded to Hold.
- Target price: ₹737.

**Q2 FY27 Financial Performance**
- Consolidated EBITDA growth: 27% YoY.
- EBITDA growth missed estimates by 3%.
- Domestic volume growth: 10%.
- Parachute volume growth: 13%.
- Parachute value growth remained at 1%.

**FY27 Guidance & Revenue Outlook**
- FY27 EBITDA growth guidance raised to mid-20s.
- Earlier EBITDA growth guidance: Around 20%.
- FY27 sales expected to comfortably exceed ₹15,000 Cr.

**Key Growth Drivers**
- Procurement benefits improve cost visibility.
- Project SETU supports General Trade transformation.
- Growth businesses improving profitability.
- Strong execution supports higher EBITDA guidance.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong volume growth supports business momentum.
- Parachute volume growth exceeded value growth.
- Higher procurement benefits support margin outlook.
- FY27 EBITDA guidance raised significantly.
- Impact: **Positive**

**JEFFERIES – MARICO LIMITED**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target price: ₹1,035.

**Growth & Operating Performance**
- Volume and EBITDA growth reached multi-year highs.
- Core portfolio delivered strong growth.
- Parachute and VAHO performed strongly.
- Foods and PPC supported growth momentum.

**FY27 Guidance & Revenue Ambition**
- Management raised FY27 guidance.
- ₹20,000 Cr revenue target advanced by one year.
- Earlier target timeline: FY30.
- New target timeline: FY29.

**Competitive Positioning & Valuation**
- Marico outperforms peers on growth consistency.
- Several peers face uneven business trends.
- Strong compounding performance supports premium valuation.
- Valuation remains higher relative to peers.

**Key Takeaway**
- Core brands continue delivering strong growth.
- Foods and PPC strengthen diversification.
- Revenue ambition advanced by one year.
- Premium valuation reflects consistent compounding.
- Impact: **Positive**

**HSBC – MARICO LIMITED**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target price: ₹1,080.

**Q2 FY27 Financial Performance**
- Results broadly in line with estimates.
- EBITDA growth: 27% YoY.

**FY27 Earnings Outlook**
- FY27 EBITDA growth guidance raised.
- Revised EBITDA growth guidance: Mid-20s.
- Among the highest growth outlooks in HSBC coverage.

**Business Expansion & Growth**
- Foods business continues scaling up.
- Premium Personal Care business expanding.
- FY29 revenue ambition: ₹20,000 Cr.
- Earlier revenue target: FY30.

**Key Takeaway**
- Strong EBITDA growth supports earnings momentum.
- Foods and Premium Personal Care expanding.
- Revenue ambition advanced by one year.
- Growth and diversification support potential rerating.
- Impact: **Positive**

**CLSA – ITC LIMITED**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Outperform.
- Target price: ₹390.

**Standalone Financial Performance**
- Net revenue growth: 3% YoY.
- EBITDA declined 17% YoY.
- Unprecedented cigarette tax increase impacted profitability.

**Cigarette Business Performance**
- Q2 cigarette net revenue declined 21% YoY.
- Cigarette EBIT declined 27% YoY.
- Cigarette EBIT exceeded expectations by 4%.
- Management adopted calibrated pricing responses.
- Multiple portfolio interventions implemented.
- Focus remains on limiting illicit trade migration.

**Non-Cigarette Business Performance**
- Segment revenue increased 18% YoY.
- Segment EBITDA increased 23% YoY.
- FMCG business led segment growth.
- Paperboards business witnessed recovery.
- Agriculture business delivered strong performance.

**Key Takeaway**
- Cigarette tax hikes pressured overall profitability.
- Non-cigarette businesses delivered strong growth.
- Portfolio interventions aim to protect cigarette volumes.
- Impact: **Mixed**

**JEFFERIES – ITC LIMITED**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target price: ₹350.

**Cigarette Business Performance**
- Cigarette volumes and EBIT continue declining.
- Sharp tax hikes pressure cigarette business.
- Management undertaking measures to navigate challenges.
- Significant illicit cigarette tax arbitrage persists.
- Calibrated price hikes expected to support recovery.
- Sequential improvement in cigarette trends expected.

**Non-Cigarette Business Performance**
- FMCG delivered strong Q2 performance.
- Paperboards reported strong Q2 performance.
- Agriculture business performance remained in line.

**Earnings Estimates & Outlook**
- EPS estimates trimmed by 2–3%.
- Gradual cigarette business recovery expected.
- Pricing actions should support sequential improvement.

**Key Takeaway**
- FMCG and Paperboards remain key growth drivers.
- Cigarette business continues facing tax-related pressure.
- Calibrated pricing may support gradual recovery.
- Jefferies retains Buy rating despite EPS cuts.
- Impact: **Mixed to Positive**

**GOLDMAN SACHS – ITC LIMITED**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Neutral.
- Target price: ₹290.

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- Q2 performance broadly matched estimates.
- Non-cigarette businesses accelerated growth.
- FMCG delivered strong revenue and margin performance.
- Paper business reported strong revenue and margins.

**Cigarette Business Performance**
- Cigarette EBIT declined 27% YoY.
- EBIT decline showed gradual moderation.
- Recovery expected to remain gradual.

**Key Takeaway**
- Non-cigarette businesses supported overall performance.
- FMCG and Paper delivered strong results.
- Cigarette profitability remains under pressure.
- Gradual cigarette business recovery remains expected.
- Impact: **Mixed**

**JPMORGAN – ITC LIMITED**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Neutral.
- Target price: ₹310.

**Q2 FY27 Financial Performance**
- EBITDA exceeded estimates by 3%.
- Non-cigarette businesses delivered better-than-expected performance.
- Cigarette operational performance remained broadly in line.

**Cigarette Business Performance**
- Cigarette EBIT declined 27% YoY.
- Delayed price hikes impacted profitability.
- Cigarette volumes declined 7–8%.
- Portfolio mix reset is currently underway.
- RSFT and DSFT salience nearly converged.

**Pricing Strategy & Margin Outlook**
- Portfolio restructuring continues.
- Staggered pricing actions expected to narrow EBIT decline.
- Further pricing actions likely, particularly in RSFT.
- EBIT expected to stabilise by Q4.

**Key Takeaway**
- Non-cigarette businesses supported EBITDA performance.
- Cigarette profitability remains under pressure.
- Pricing actions may support gradual recovery.
- EBIT stabilisation expected by Q4.
- Impact: **Mixed**

**HSBC – UPL LIMITED**

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- Q2 FY27 performance exceeded estimates.
- Crop Protection faced operational headwinds.
- Advanta delivered strong performance.
- Specialty Chemicals also performed well.

**FY27 Guidance**
- Revenue growth guidance retained.
- EBITDA growth guidance retained.
- No definitive update on reorganisation.

**Valuation**
- UPL trades at 5.3x FY28E EV/EBITDA.

**Key Takeaway**
- Advanta and Specialty Chemicals supported performance.
- Crop Protection remained under pressure.
- FY27 growth guidance remains unchanged.
- Reorganisation update remains awaited.
- Impact: **Positive**

**JEFFERIES – UPL LIMITED**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Buy.
- Target price: ₹610.

**Q2 FY27 Financial Performance**
- Revenue broadly in line with estimates.
- EBITDA and PAT exceeded Jefferies estimates.
- Revenue remained flat YoY.
- Adverse weather impacted sales volumes.
- Foreign exchange movements supported revenue performance.

**Segment Performance**
- Advanta delivered strong EBITDA growth.
- UPL SAS also reported strong EBITDA growth.

**Balance Sheet & Working Capital**
- Working capital increased YoY.
- Net debt expanded YoY.

**FY27 Outlook & Guidance**
- Management maintained FY27 guidance.
- Guidance implies mid-teens growth in H2 FY27.
- Jefferies projects 15% FY27 EBITDA growth.

**Valuation & Stock Performance**
- Stock corrected 35% since restructuring announcement.

**Key Takeaway**
- EBITDA and PAT beat estimates.
- Segment profitability showed strong growth.
- Working capital and debt expansion remain monitorables.
- FY27 guidance implies stronger H2 performance.
- Impact: **Positive**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Hold.
- Target price cut to ₹2,468.

- EBITDA margin: 9.1%.
- Margin missed consensus by 160 bps.
- H1 commodity inflation reached 8–9%.
- Price hikes remained limited to 3.5–4%.
- Higher manufacturing overheads impacted margins.
- Production volumes exceeded dispatches.

- El Niño impact weighing on demand.
- High base adds further demand pressure.
- Declining demand expected for 3–4 quarters.
- FY27 domestic tractor volume forecast: Down 3%.
- H2 FY27 volume decline forecast: 16%.

**FY28 Volume Outlook**
- H1 FY28 volumes expected to remain pressured.
- Lower rainfall may impact reservoir levels.
- FY28 tractor volume forecast: Down 5%.

**Key Takeaway**
- Commodity inflation continues pressuring margins.
- Tractor demand slowdown expected to persist.
- FY27 and FY28 volume outlook remains weak.
- Margin recovery and rural demand need monitoring.
- Impact: **Negative**

- Earlier guidance: Mid-single-digit growth.

- Another 200 bps commodity cost impact expected.
- Impact expected during Q3 FY27.
- Pricing actions expected to support recovery.

- Potential El Niño impact on demand.
- Timing and pace of margin recovery.

**Key Takeaway**
- Tractor volume outlook has weakened significantly.
- Commodity inflation continues pressuring margins.
- Pricing actions may support Q4 recovery.
- Demand slowdown and margin recovery need monitoring.

- Asset quality remains healthy.
- Valuation stands at 0.5x FY28 P/BV.

- Franchise capable of sustaining 1.6% RoA.

**Key Takeaway**
- PAT growth benefited from provision write-back.
- Core operating performance remained relatively subdued.
- Stable margins and healthy asset quality.
- Attractive valuation supports investment thesis.
- Impact: **Mixed to Positive**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating: Outperform.
- Target price: ₹620.

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- NII reported broadly in line with estimates.
- PAT exceeded estimates by 15%.
- Recoveries from written-off accounts aided profitability.
- Negative credit costs supported PAT performance.

**Margins & Lending Rates**
- NIM remained stable QoQ.
- Prime lending rate increased by 25 bps.
- Rate hike should support margins.
- Incremental lending yields remain 70 bps lower.
- Comparison is against overall portfolio yields.

**Loan Growth & Disbursements**
- Disbursement growth improved over three quarters.
- Overall loan growth remains modest at 4–5%.

**Business Strategy**
- Increasing focus on higher-yielding lending segments.
- Loans against property gaining strategic focus.
- Prime housing faces intense bank competition.

**Key Takeaway**
- PAT beat was supported by recoveries.
- Lending rate increase may support margins.
- Loan growth remains relatively subdued.
- LAP focus targets higher lending yields.
- Impact: **Mixed**

**BOFA SECURITIES – ESCORTS KUBOTA DOWNGRADE**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating downgraded to Underperform.
- Target price cut to ₹2,100.
- Earlier target price: ₹3,500.

**Q2 FY27 Performance & Margin Pressure**
- Q2 performance missed estimates.
- Margins declined 300 bps QoQ.
- Sharp margin squeeze driven by metal inflation.
- Metals account for 11–12% of net revenue.
- Margin pressure remains unresolved.

**Tractor Industry Outlook**
- Management commentary signals deeper tractor downcycle.
- Expects double-digit decline during H2.
- FY27 growth outlook turns marginally negative.
- Earlier FY27 growth expectation: 4–5%.

**Earnings & Valuation Concerns**
- EPS estimates cut by 11–13%.
- Weak growth and margin pressure drive downgrades.
- Further valuation downside remains possible.
- Stock valuations remain unattractive versus peers.

**Key Takeaway**
- BOFA sees worsening tractor industry conditions.
- Metal inflation continues pressuring margins.
- Earnings estimates face significant downward revisions.
- Valuation concerns reinforce the downgrade.
- Impact: **Negative**

**KOTAK INSTITUTIONAL EQUITIES – ESCORTS KUBOTA**

**Rating & Target Price**
- Rating upgraded to Buy.
- Target price: ₹3,100.
- Recommendation: Look beyond near-term weakness.

**Q2 FY27 Performance**
- Standalone EBITDA missed estimates by 10.9%.
- Higher employee expenses impacted performance.
- Manufacturing overheads exceeded expectations.

**Growth Outlook**
- Expects outperformance against tractor industry.
- Multiple product launches to drive growth.
- Favourable geographical exposure supports performance.
- Margins expected to recover gradually from CY2027E.
- Construction equipment demand momentum remains steady.

**Business Diversification**
- Expanding presence across spares and engines.
- Agri-solutions broadening the revenue base.
- Diversification should reduce business cyclicality.

**Valuation & Investment View**
- Recent stock correction improved valuation attractiveness.
- Current market price offers attractive valuations.

**Key Takeaway**
- Near-term earnings faced cost-related pressure.
- Product launches support future tractor growth.
- Margin recovery expected from CY2027E.
- Diversification supports long-term business resilience.
- Impact: **Positive**

**HSBC – PRIVATE BANKS SECTOR OUTLOOK**

**Preferred Banks & Ratings**
- Preferred picks: ICICI Bank, Axis Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank.

Curious when FII will come back to India

So gave Co-pilot a prompt
“Why FIIs wont return to India even as AI trade unwind globally”

Reverse Psychology

Here is the response

1. India is still expensive vs EM peers
o Even after corrections, India trades at a premium to most emerging markets.
o FIIs compare India with China, Korea, Taiwan, Brazil, not with India's own history.
o If China is at 10-12x PE and India at 20-25x PE, capital tends to chase cheaper markets. 
2. India lacks direct AI beneficiaries
o The AI trade created winners in US tech, Taiwan semiconductors and Korean memory-chip companies.
o India has very few large listed AI, semiconductor or hyperscaler plays that global thematic funds can buy. 
3. Dollar returns matter, not rupee returns
o FIIs think in USD.
o Even if Nifty is flat or slightly up, rupee depreciation can wipe out returns.
o Currency risk remains a major deterrent for foreign capital. 
4. US yields remain a strong competitor
o If US Treasuries offer attractive risk-free returns, FIIs need a much higher expected return from India.
o Many global allocators prefer earning 4-5% in dollar assets rather than taking EM risk. 
5. India's earnings growth has moderated
o India's premium valuation was justified when earnings were compounding rapidly.
o If earnings growth slows while valuations remain rich, FIIs question the risk-reward. 
6. Better opportunities elsewhere
o Korea, Taiwan and China offer exposure to AI, semiconductors and manufacturing at lower valuations.
o Global funds have finite capital; India is competing against these markets for allocation. 
7. India is no longer an under-owned market
o After years of strong inflows, most EM funds already have meaningful India exposure.
o Incremental flows require a new catalyst, not just the absence of AI enthusiasm.
8. Domestic flows reduce urgency
o SIPs, mutual funds and insurance money continue supporting Indian markets despite FII selling.
o Paradoxically, this resilience prevents large valuation corrections that would otherwise attract FIIs back.

Maruti Suzuki India should be rechristened as Suzuki India

Maruti's journey started as a Govt of India project. Maruti Udyog was the Indian promoter & Suzuki was brought in as the technology partner. Back then, this was very much an Indian company with Japanese know-how.

Over time, the Indian promoter gradually diluted its holding & eventually exited completely. Suzuki did the opposite, staying invested through every cycle & steadily increasing its stake.

What began as a JV slowly became Suzuki's most important global asset. The ownership story itself tells you who has deepened commitment over the decades.

For years, investors debated why Suzuki was setting up fresh manufacturing capacity outside Maruti Suzuki through its Gujarat subsidiary instead of housing it directly in the listed entity.

Then came the reversal. Suzuki transferred Suzuki Motor Gujarat into Maruti Suzuki at a valuation of roughly ₹12,000+ Cr. Rather than taking cash, it largely took equity.

The result? Suzuki's ownership in Maruti Suzuki moved up further without having to buy equivalent shares from the secondary market.

This wasn't just a restructuring exercise. It was Suzuki effectively converting manufacturing assets into a larger stake in India's largest PV company.

Even after that transaction, Suzuki did not stop. It has periodically picked up additional shares from the open market whenever opportunities emerged.

The message is clear. The Indian promoter exited long ago. The Japanese promoter keeps doubling down on India.

Look at the cars on the road today. The branding emphasis is on the giant "S" logo. 10-15years back, cars started selling with only “S” logo, 1st on premium nexa cars, then on all the models. You will hardly see Maruti branded cars on road now

For many younger buyers, the brand recall is shifting from "Maruti Suzuki" to simply "Suzuki". The transition is subtle but visible.

India is now the crown jewel of Suzuki Motor Corp. A substantial portion of Suzuki valuation come from Indian listed entity. Maruti $38bn mcap translate to $21bn (for 58% stake, $15bn if applied 30% Holdco disc).

Even beyond that, Maruti pays over $500m to Suzuki as royalty, that value must be over $5bn in the SoTP of Suzuki motors. Suzuki motors also have successful 2w biz in India, they are 6th largest 2w in India, clocking over 1lac units every month

In many ways, investors buying Suzuki Motor Corp are indirectly buying the India story. Cars sold by Suzuki in India is higher than overall car sold by Suzuki in other 100 countries combined

A rebranding to "Suzuki India" could also help shed the old "cheap small-car company" perception. As premium SUVs, hybrids & future EVs gain share, a stronger global MNC identity may command a different customer mindset.

Ownership, capital allocation, manufacturing integration, branding & growth strategy all point in one direction: this is increasingly Suzuki's India story.

Conclusion: Maruti only stays in Co. name hence should be renamed now
